title: Science & Nature Explorers
subject: Science & Nature
description: Fascinating questions about plants, water cycles, forces, weather, and our living planet.

questions.question: What gas do green plants absorb from the air during photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Plants take in carbon dioxide and water with sunlight to produce oxygen and glucose!

questions.question: What is the boiling point of pure water at sea level?
questions.fact: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) under standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Which of these is the hardest natural mineral found on Earth?
questions.fact: Diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, making it the hardest natural mineral.

questions.question: What force pulls dropped objects toward the center of the Earth?
questions.fact: Gravity is the invisible force that attracts objects toward each other.

questions.question: What part of a plant absorbs water and nutrients from the soil?
questions.fact: Roots anchor the plant firmly in the ground and draw up essential moisture and minerals.

questions.question: Which state of matter has a definite shape and a definite volume?
questions.fact: In solids, molecules are packed closely together in a rigid, fixed arrangement.

questions.question: What color appears at the very top outer edge of a standard rainbow?
questions.fact: Rainbow colors follow ROYGBIV: Red is at the top because it has the longest wavelength!

questions.question: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.fact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, but many fuse together as they grow to 206 bones in adulthood.

questions.question: What is the process called when water vapor cools down and turns back into liquid water droplets?
questions.fact: Condensation creates clouds in the sky and dew on morning grass.

questions.question: Which organ in the human body pumps blood through all your blood vessels?
questions.fact: Your heart beats about 100,000 times each day to circulate oxygen-rich blood.

questions.question: What instrument is used to measure air temperature?
questions.fact: A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.

questions.question: Which type of animal can live both on land and in water?
questions.fact: Amphibians like frogs and salamanders start life breathing in water through gills and develop lungs to live on land!

questions.question: What is the layer of gases surrounding Earth called?
questions.fact: The atmosphere shields Earth from space radiation and gives us air to breathe.

questions.question: What substance makes plant leaves look green?
questions.fact: Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into food.

questions.question: Sound travels fastest through which of the following?
questions.fact: Sound waves need particles to vibrate; closely packed solid particles transmit sound much faster than liquids or gases!

questions.question: What natural event is measured using the Richter scale?
questions.fact: The Richter scale calculates the seismic energy and magnitude released by an earthquake.
